vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2464: feat(dashboard): Machine Room — complete /resources overhaul (attribution, reclaim advisor, stop/pause, disk, spawn-gate visibility)

plan.title: feat(dashboard): Machine Room — complete /resources overhaul (attribution, reclaim advisor, stop/pause, disk, spawn-gate visibility)
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: The current /resources page shows a flat container list with CPU/mem and start/restart only. Operations exposed every gap at once: 9 GB held by stacks of already-merged issues (no reclaim surface, no stop button), a container OOM-thrashing at its 4 GB limit with no limit visibility, a load-45 vitest spike with no attribution, mystery spawn-gate 409s, and 52 GB of orphaned TLDR venvs invisible to the UI.
narratives.Proposal: Rebuild /resources as the Machine Room per the binding mockup: host vitals strip with spawn-gate state, pipeline-aware reclaim advisor, issue-grouped stack cards with limit awareness and the full verb set (start/stop/pause/restart/logs/terminal/tear-down), agents section with process-tree stats and burn rate, core services and host-process attribution, and a 24h annotated history with capacity forecast. All data flows through the extended /api/resources read door (D1); resources.ts splits into a routes/resources/ module folder; grouping, reclaim logic, and burn math are server-side.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No new state plane and no direct DB/GitHub access from the frontend — pipeline state via the review-status resolver only (D3)
- Tear-down never deletes the git worktree — docker containers/volumes/networks only (D4)
- No continuous per-process history — spike-attribution snapshots only (D6)
- No ML forecasting — heuristic last-run peak / fleet median only (D7)
- No changes to spawn-gate enforcement behavior — this issue only surfaces the existing verdict
- No mobile/responsive redesign — mockup targets 1440px desktop
- No removal or behavior change of the 11 existing /api/resources endpoints (no-loss audit enforces this)
- No raising of memory limits automatically — 'Raise limit' only opens the compose override editor path

autoDecisions.summary: Corrected the PRD's evaluateSpawnGuardrails reference: the function is defined in src/dashboard/server/routes/agents/shared.ts:548; spawn.ts:341 is the call site. Gate mapping: 200+no-warnings=OPEN, requiresAcknowledgement=SOFT, blocked=BLOCKED.
autoDecisions.rationale: Verified by grep during discovery; the PRD cited the call site. Recording the definition site prevents the work agent hunting for a function that isn't in spawn.ts.

autoDecisions.summary: Teardown endpoint reuses only docker-scoped steps (stopDocker + compose down -v equivalent), never teardownWorkspace() wholesale.
autoDecisions.rationale: teardownWorkspace() calls removeWorktree (teardown-workspace.ts:375), which deletes the git worktree — directly violating D4's 'Tear-down NEVER deletes the git worktree'. The PRD said 'through the existing teardown lib'; the safe reading is its docker steps only.

autoDecisions.summary: Single issue with one mega-vBRIEF (22 beads) rather than sibling issues; two foundation server beads then vertical slices, with snapshot.ts-touching beads marked readiness:sequential.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD's Sequencing section explicitly suggests a single work agent with server phases before UI; the beads share one payload contract (snapshot.ts) and one page shell, so parallel dispatch would conflict on shared files — sequential is the honest readiness.

autoDecisions.summary: Frontend rework lands in a new src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/resources/ module folder with ResourcesPanel.tsx remaining the mounted entry.
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps the '/resources' route mounting (App/routes.ts, AppRoutes.tsx) untouched, satisfies the file-size ceiling, and gives the six UI beads mostly disjoint files_scope.

autoDecisions.summary: Live refresh extends the existing resources.updated emitOnly domain-event path on the DockerStatsCollector 5s cadence; polling is only the WS-down fallback.
autoDecisions.rationale: Discovery showed the frontend is already event-driven (EventRouter -> Zustand -> useResourceStats); adding a parallel polling loop would duplicate the read path and raise event-loop load (NFR-1).

Each stack carries: issueId, issueTitle, composeProject, serviceCount, per-service rows (reusing ContainerStats from DockerStatsCollector.getStats()), aggregates (CPU%, RAM bytes, disk = volumes+layers via batched docker system df / inspect on the collector cadence, NOT per-request), and pipeline phase resolved via the review-status read door (getReviewStatusSync / cached loadReviewStatuses — same phase vocabulary as getPipelineIssuePhase in src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/pipeline-state.ts). narrative.Action: Add GET /api/resources/stacks/:issueId/teardown-estimate returning {ramBytes, diskBytes, confirmToken} where the estimate sums the stack's live RAM plus volumes+layers disk, and confirmToken is a short-lived server-generated token bound to the issueId. Reclaim advisor server logic: pipeline-aware safe-to-free candidates

expected_outputs: typecheck completes without errors

narrative.Action: Add reclaim.ts computing reclaimCandidates[] in the payload (D3): (a) merged/closed-issue stacks still running or holding disk — issue state via the review-status resolver, blocked if any live agent session references the issue (listAgentStates + tmux liveness); (b) orphaned workspace TLDR .venv directories >1 GB whose issue is closed (scan workspaces/*/.venv sizes on the collector cadence, cached); (c) dangling volumes + build cache (docker system df / volume ls -f dangling=true); (d) exited containers. Each candidate: {kind, label, why, ramBytes, diskBytes, action} where action names the endpoint the UI calls (stack stop, venv delete, prune, remove). Include totals; the UI hides the advisor when total < 500 MB (threshold shipped in payload so server owns the rule). Add DELETE /api/resources/venvs/:issue for the venv candidate (validates the issue is closed server-side before rm). All scanning batched on the collector cadence, never per-request. Sequential: shares snapshot.ts with sibling payload beads.

Spike-attribution sampler: snapshot top processes into one annotation event when host CPU spikes

expected_outputs: typecheck completes without errors

narrative.Action: Add spike-sampler.ts hooked to the collector cadence (D6): when host CPU or 1-min load crosses a threshold (default CPU >80% or load > cores×1.5) and no spike episode is open, snapshot the top-3 process groups from the shared ps parse and write ONE activity.entry via emitActivityEntrySync (activity-logger.ts:107) with details.category='resources', message naming the top culprits (e.g. 'Load 45 spike — vitest ×10 workers (agent-pan-2341-test)'), and the attribution ids. The episode closes when the metric drops below threshold−hysteresis for 2 ticks; a new episode may then open. No continuous per-process history is stored. All tests use fake timers.

narrative.Action: Add forecast.ts (D7): record each stack's peak RAM and average CPU while running (from the collector cadence) and persist the peak on stack stop/teardown as a small JSON sidecar in the server's state dir (or reuse an existing lightweight KV if one exists in the routes' reach — NOT a new SQLite table). Reclaim advisor UI: candidate rows, per-line actions, streamed Reclaim-all-safe

expected_outputs: typecheck completes without errors

narrative.Action: Render the reclaim advisor block (the page hero, mockup rule 2) from snapshot.reclaimCandidates: header with RAM+disk totals and 'Reclaim all safe', one row per candidate with label, why-text, amount, and its action button (Stop stack → stack-verbs stop; Delete venvs → venv DELETE; Prune → existing prune endpoints; Remove → existing container delete). Advisor hidden when totals are under the server-shipped threshold.
